topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: They said it was her ring, the one she wore when she said yes to a life. The pawn shop's a cold place, where things end up when money gets tight and the heart's too heavy to hold on. I gave it a once-over, noted the wear, the patina of years. "Looks like it," I told her, though I knew by the way she held herself it was more than just a hunch. People bring me things they can't explain, secrets wrapped in stories. This was one of those, a piece of her past reclaimed from the shadows. I kept my eyes on the ring while she paid, didn’t say much, just watched the rain outside, falling like the world was washing its hands of everything.
